cases.description: Valid registry for example.com/finance-other/loan-rules, outside repository namespace example.com/finance. All pins, signatures and bytes otherwise valid.
The only consumer DSSE signature is by the repository targets role key, which is absent from the publisher rule. TUF authorization remains valid.
Consumer DSSE payloadType application/vnd.example.other+json with a valid Ed25519 signature over that exact wrong type. Valid TUF hashes and lock pins.
Consumer envelope has two signatures and different keyid hints by publisher-a only; publisher threshold is two distinct raw keys.
Repository-authenticated envelope bytes have no valid authorized publisher signature.
A real successful fresh restore creates A's grants. Expired metadata and withheld registry permit exact continued use under previous-authorization.
A independently earns grants. B starts with the same fixed lock and copied ordinary bytes but explicitly initialized security. At timestamp expiry, B fails first restore.
A's prior grant does not bypass the current strict freshness policy at expiry.
Removing current repository authority immediately blocks a valid previous grant.
Removing the effective publisher rule immediately blocks previous authorization.
Removing publisher-a retains continued use because publisher-b verified at grant creation and meets current threshold.
A and B earn independent grants, explicitly refresh a fresh revocation view, then both reject offline continued use.
A has a valid old grant but receives no revoked view; no promise of learning offline revocations is made.
Fresh authorization fails at exact timestamp expiry, using one fixed UTC clock.
A successful fresh restore records its clock; an earlier operation cannot establish new freshness.
Missing retained targets bytes are availability failure, not signature failure.
Sequential old/new threshold root rotation preserves repository identity and existing grants.
A current version-2 view establishes timestamp floor 2; an explicit refresh of older view-one rejects rollback.
A new client provisioned at root 2 authenticates old lock evidence using supplied original root bytes and its forward authenticated chain.
Fresh root-2 authorization cannot replace missing original root bytes required by the old lock.
